Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited. Procurement here needs a concrete sequencing plan so legal and finance can align on deadlines. High level constraints:

- Pilot go-live target: 2028-06-01 (hard).
- MedNova legal requires SOC2 evidence and DPA signed before any production data flows.
- Our finance team needs an executed order form + billing contact in your system before we can cut the PO.

Can you share a mutual action plan that maps the MSA, DPA, and Order Form dependencies with milestone dates and owners? Would like to see:
- who reviews the DPA vs MSA in parallel vs sequentially
- expected legal turnaround times (MedNova typically needs 7 business days for each redline review)
- a fallback plan if SOC2 evidence gating slips by >2 weeks

If possible, send a single-sheet MAP and a short timeline (2 pages max). Wed like to circulate to our legal and procurement leads today.

Thanks,

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clarity and timeline. I put a first-pass MAP together (attached) that reflects the dependencies you called out. Key points up front:

- We can run MSA and DPA reviews in parallel, but execution (signature) must follow the order form completion to enable billing. That means procurement + finance need the final order form in circulation at least 7 business days before your target PO date.
- SOC2 evidence (well provide our latest attestations and the security pack) is a hard gate for production; for the pilot we can provide a scoped, non-production data allowance under the same DPA with controls.
- Proposed milestone slate: Legal review cycle 1 complete by 2028-03-24; Order form ready for sign by 2028-04-05; Final execution by 2028-04-12 to keep ramp on schedule.

Im looping in Karthik (legal) to confirm sequencing assumptions and provide redline guidance, and Laura for sales-level approval on discounting/effective dates.

Hi Samantha / Priyom — thanks for the MAP draft. A few legal/contract sequencing clarifications from our side: 

1) Parallel review is fine: our legal team can review MSA and DPA in parallel to shorten calendar time. Caveat: any material MSA change that affects data handling (clauses around data residency, breach notification) will ripple into DPA language and require a follow-up DPA review cycle.

2) Order form must be final prior to countersignature only because the order form contains term- and billing-specific variables (term length, seat counts, unit prices, start date) that create commercial obligations. We can provision trial access before execution if you list the environment as 'pilot' and accept limited SLA.

3) Redline expectations: we generally turn initial redlines around in 3-5 business days; follow-up rounds vary. Given your 7-business-day baseline, the proposed dates look achievable if both sides keep to single-cycle redlining where possible.

I attached a short checklist (DPA-checklist.docx) with questions we will send to your privacy lead; please identify the MedNova privacy contact so we can avoid back-and-forth. Also attached MSA_redlines_KI_comments.pdf with high-level flags (data residency, subprocessors, indemnity cap point).

Proposed minor schedule tweak: shift Order Form ready-for-sign to 2028-04-03 to allow one additional internal review day. That keeps final execution by 2028-04-10—still ahead of your 06-01 pilot date and gives space for finance to issue PO.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
